typeIdent.description:
Indicates explicit sub-type of entry.  Composed of the concatenation of the typeKey of the instance's type and all
of its base type's typeIdent

id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

srcType.description: The source type for this spec (e.g. the type on which `evalMetrics` will be called).

dataTimestamp.description:
The last time when data was persisted for this spec.
For a spec attached to an {@link MLTrainingJob} this timestamp reflects the time at which the job that persisted
the data completed. Note that there will not be any data associated with that instance of the spec, but rather
with the corresponding specs attached to all of the trained pipelines.
For a spec attached to an {@link MLPipeline} this timestamp reflects the actual time at which the data for that
was persisted as part of the training job.

target.description: Identifier for the target to learn

features.description: Names of metrics to use in training

maskMetric.description:
If specified, data samples (each data sample corresponds to a source + time) where `maskMetric` is non-zero
will be removed from the data.  Specific subTypes (e.g. outputting {@link Dataset}s or {@link Tensor}s) may use
this field slightly differently.  See the documentation of this field on those Types.

overrideSimpleMetrics.description: Simple Metrics not previously defined in the platform

overrideCompoundMetrics.description: Compound Metrics not previously defined in the platform

startPath.description:
Path from source object to timestamp from which the features need to be extracted.
Refer to the type level documentation for how this field affects the evaluated start date.

start.description:
Default start time from which the features will be extracted.
Refer to the type level documentation for how this field affects the evaluated start date.

endPath.description:
Path from source object to timestamp until which the features need to be extracted.
Refer to the type level documentation for how this field affects the evaluated end date.

end.description:
Default end time until which the features will be extracted.
Refer to the type level documentation for how this field affects the evaluated end date.

intervalsFromStartToEnd.description:
Number of intervals between start and end date of the evalMetrics call.
Refer to the type level documentation for how this field affects the evaluated start or end date.

interval.description: Interval to use to extract data between start and end dates.

title:
{@link SupervisedMLDataSourceSpec} that creates {@link EvalMetricsSpec}s for each source object.

The following table shows what values will be used for the {@link EvalMetricsSpec#start} and {@link EvalMetricsSpec#end} fields
given various combinations of {@link start}, {@link end}, {@link startPath}, {@link endPath}, and {@link intervalsFromStartToEnd}.
When defined, {@link startPath} and {@link endPath} take precedence over {@link start} and {@link end},
allowing per-instance evaluated start and end based on the value at {@link startPath} and/or {@link endPath}.
Note that for {@link startPath} or {@link endPath} to be considered 'Defined' in the table below, {@link startPath} must be set to a valid
field path on the spec *and* must lead to a defined `datetime` value on the source object being evaluated.
If the evaluated end for a given source object is earlier than the evaluated start, then an error message will be
logged and no data will be evaluated for that source.

NOTE:
 `intervalsFromStartToEnd` must be a positive integer if defined.
 In addition, defining `intervalsFromStartToEnd` while leaving `startPath` and `endPath` undefined on the spec is an
 invalid configuration and will result in an error message and no metric evaluation.
 Defining `intervalsFromStartToEnd`, `startPath`, and `endPath` all together is also an invalid configuration.

| start    | end      | startPath | endPath   | intervalsFromStartToEnd | evaluated start                   | evaluated end                          |
|----------|----------|-----------|-----------|-------------------------|-----------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| Required | Required | Defined   | Defined   | Undefined               | startPath                         | endPath                                |
| Required | Required | Defined   | Undefined | Positive                | startPath                         | startPath + intervalsFromStartToEnd    |
| Required | Required | Defined   | Undefined | Undefined               | startPath                         | end                                    |
| Required | Required | Undefined | Defined   | Positive                | endPath - intervalsFromStartToEnd | endPath                                |
| Required | Required | Undefined | Defined   | Undefined               | start                             | endPath                                |
| Required | Required | Undefined | Undefined | Undefined               | start                             | end                                    |
name: AbstractEvalMetricsMLDataSourceSpec
